title: Project
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 9 Pre-Technical Studies; not yet checked by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher; safety lines marked SAFETY in the library to confirm first; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Making the item (outcome c) is marked with the KICD rubric on the item and the learner's folio; the questions test planning, order and evaluation.

skills.key_step: The learner identifies a problem in the locality that Pre-Technical skills can solve, selects an item to make, and orders the project steps: identify the problem, choose the item, plan (drawing, materials, cost), make, test, evaluate and improve.

floor.question: Name one source of a business idea.

representations: a problem and item matching card
steps: Choose an item that solves it.
Check it suits skills and materials.

board.do: Write the problem: "shoes lie on the classroom floor".

board.say: What item could solve this, using local materials?

board.do: Wait for the learner to say a shoe rack from offcuts.
Write the project steps in order.

misconceptions.ask: What is the first step of a project?
misconceptions.repair: Order the project steps on cards: identify a problem, choose an item, plan, make, test, evaluate.

misconceptions.ask: After making the item, what comes next?
misconceptions.repair: Test a made item against its purpose (does the rack hold the shoes?) and improve it before handing in.

misconceptions.ask: Which materials are best for a school project?
misconceptions.repair: List local and waste materials (offcuts, bottles, sisal, scrap metal) and items made from them.

listen_for: Build a new road for the village
misconceptions.ask: Which problem suits a Grade 9 Pre-Technical project?
misconceptions.repair: Check each idea against skills, tools, time and money; shrink a big idea into a small item that helps.

checks.question: What is the first step of a project?
What comes after making the item?

skills.key_step: The learner plans and evaluates the making of a project item from local materials: sketch and working drawing, materials and cost list, order of operations (mark, cut, join, sand, finish), safe use of tools, testing and evaluation against the problem; the item and folio are marked with the rubric.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the steps of a project.
floor.question: What is the first step of a project?

representations: an evaluation checklist tied to the problem
contexts: a shoe rack for the classroom
a bird feeder from waste materials

board.do: Write the order cards: finish, cut, mark, join, sand.
Wait for the learner to say last.
Put all the cards in order.

misconceptions.ask: What should you prepare before you start making a project item?
misconceptions.repair: Show two shelves: one made from a drawing, one without; compare the fit and the waste.

listen_for: It is a waste of time
misconceptions.ask: Why list the materials and their cost before starting?
misconceptions.repair: Cost a small item together (timber, nails, glue, varnish); compare with the money available.

listen_for: Before cutting and joining the parts
misconceptions.ask: When is a wooden item painted or varnished?
misconceptions.repair: Show how glue does not stick to varnish and cutting damages the finish; write the order of operations.

misconceptions.ask: How is a finished project item evaluated?
misconceptions.repair: Return to the problem statement; test the item against it (does the shoe rack hold 20 pairs?) and list improvements.

checks.question: What is prepared before making an item?
checks.answer: A sketch and working drawing with sizes

checks.question: How is the item evaluated?
checks.answer: By whether it solves the problem
